title: Seven unique random numbers
description:
Write a function which returns an array of seven random numbers in a range of 0-9. All the numbers must be unique.

Python-Gym adaptation: since the source exercise names no function, implement as unique_random_numbers(seed=None). When seed is provided, seed the random module with it first. Return a list of seven distinct integers, each in the range 0-9 inclusive.
starter_code:
import random

def unique_random_numbers(seed=None):
    # your code here
    pass
hints: random.sample() picks a given number of unique elements from a population without repeats, unlike random.choice() which can repeat.
The available range 0-9 has exactly 10 numbers, and you need 7 unique ones from it, so random.sample(range(10), 7) is a natural fit.
Seed random first (only if seed is not None), then return random.sample(range(10), 7) as the list of seven unique numbers.
expected_behavior: Returns a list of 7 integers, each between 0 and 9 inclusive, with no repeated values. With the same seed, the returned list is always identical.

hidden_tests.label: seed 0 produces the expected deterministic list of 7 unique numbers
seed 1 produces the expected deterministic list of 7 unique numbers

explanation: random.sample(range(10), 7) draws 7 distinct values without replacement from the 10 possible numbers 0-9, which directly satisfies the uniqueness requirement; seeding random beforehand makes the drawn sample reproducible.
